title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: MARNIE'S DOGS
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Marnie Fitch, a baggage handler at the airport in Fairbanks, Alaska.
In winter, she never leaves her couch.
Then one morning, six dogs showed up on her porch.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: SIX DOGS
segments.quote: All adventures, especially into new territory, are scary.
segments.author: Sally Ride
lines: Her neighbor Ole, a seventy-nine-year-old sled dog racer, was moving to Arizona for his knees.
He handed her six old dogs, a sled, and a note from the astronaut Sally Ride:
All adventures, especially into new territory, are scary.
Marnie had never driven a sled. She had barely driven a lawn mower.
She said yes before she could talk herself out of it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: FACE IN THE SNOW
segments.quote: Never stop because you are afraid - you are never so likely to be wrong.
segments.author: Fridtjof Nansen
lines: On her first run, the dogs took off. Marnie did not.
She landed face first in a snowbank.
She nearly called Ole to take his dogs back. Then she read his next note, from the Norwegian explorer Fridtjof Nansen:
Never stop because you are afraid - you are never so likely to be wrong.
Next morning, she held on with both hands.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: PEPPER
segments.quote: Until one has loved an animal, a part of one's soul remains unawakened.
segments.author: Anatole France
lines: Her lead dog, Pepper, ignored every word she yelled.
Ole's next note came from the French writer Anatole France:
Until one has loved an animal, a part of one's soul remains unawakened.
So Marnie stopped yelling, and brushed Pepper every night.
By February, Pepper turned left the second Marnie whispered it.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: FORTY BELOW
segments.quote: Difficulties are just things to overcome, after all.
segments.author: Ernest Shackleton
lines: Then came forty below. Her truck froze. Her eyelashes froze. Her coffee froze.
She taped a line from the polar explorer Ernest Shackleton to the fridge:
Difficulties are just things to overcome, after all.
So she trained before work in the dark, sewed tiny booties, and gave her truck a blanket.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE CHECKPOINT
segments.quote: Success seems to be largely a matter of hanging on after others have let go.
segments.author: William Feather
lines: In March, she entered the Goldstream Valley thirty-mile race.
At mile fifteen, her hands were numb and her nose felt like a popsicle.
Half the teams were quitting at the checkpoint. She remembered Ole's last note, from the writer William Feather:
Success seems to be largely a matter of hanging on after others have let go.
She ate a frozen candy bar, and hung on.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE RED LANTERN
segments.quote: To give anything less than your best is to sacrifice the gift.
segments.author: Steve Prefontaine
lines: Old Biscuit got tired, so she tucked him in the sled bag and ran beside it.
Her neighbors had painted a sign with the words of the runner Steve Prefontaine:
To give anything less than your best is to sacrifice the gift.
Marnie crossed the line dead last, laughing, and won the Red Lantern, the prize for the last team in.
Ole watched on a video call, crying into his iced tea.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Say yes. Keep going. Love first. Beat the cold. Hang on. Give your best.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Say yes. Keep going when you're scared. Love first. Beat the cold. Hang on. Give your best.
Me, I tried a sled once. My dog rode. I pulled.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
